definition: Incendiary means deliberately designed to stir up open conflict or violence.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word incendiary. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know incendiary should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Stewards tore the incendiary poster off the canteen wall before the night shift arrived, but by then a hundred phones had photographed it.
A pointed remark is the mildest thing on this scale, far below incendiary — it has an edge, but it means to score a point, not to start a fire.
Provocative goes further than pointed — it is built to get a rise out of people; incendiary claims the most: language meant to end in broken glass, or worse.

Inflammatory language heats a room, and it can do so carelessly — a clumsy toast, one ill-chosen word at a dinner table, tempers rising with no plan behind them. Incendiary language is aimed: the heat is the design, chosen to end in real conflict. Every incendiary remark is inflammatory; the reverse is not true.

Rabble-rousing is done out loud and in person — a speaker working a crowd's anger, feeding on the roar that comes back. Incendiary needs no stage and no voice: a printed page or an anonymous poster can be incendiary, so long as it is built to set off the explosion.
